headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Copilot can read repo/editor context while Dagster is a non-interactive orchestrator with no direct output channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context by default, while Dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator with no clipboard, shell, or MCP surfaces. A direct injection path is not documented, but if Dagster-generated files are opened in Copilot, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dagster writes prompt-like text into repo files that Copilot opens in editor buffers, THEN instruction-following can be influenced.
IF Copilot Workspace is enabled on files produced by Dagster, THEN file content may be parsed as actionable guidance.
mitigations: Keep Dagster outputs out of files Copilot reads.
Use a separate repo or workspace for generated artifacts.
Disable Copilot Chat/Workspace on directories containing machine-generated instructions.
Add a review step before any Copilot-applied edit.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance labels on generated files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster itself has no filesystem read/write or network egress, but Copilot reads open editor buffers and repo context and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. If Dagster pipelines place sensitive data into shared files, Copilot can ingest and transmit it. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through shared workspace content.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in files that Dagster produces or transforms and Copilot opens them, THEN that data can flow to a third-party API.
IF repo context contains secrets or regulated data, THEN Copilot may transmit them during inference.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and regulated data from shared repos.
Add .gitignore and redaction rules for Dagster outputs.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive folders.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: implement DLP scanning before editor sync.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, while Copilot can write files and modify git state but only through editor-mediated edits. There is overlap on repo context, but no shared unrestricted write surface or locking conflict is documented, so the conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF a human accepts Copilot edits into the same repository Dagster manages, THEN concurrent changes can collide.
IF multiple Copilot instances edit the same files without review, THEN git conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Stagger Dagster runs and editor sessions.
Use branch-per-task workflows.
Review Copilot diffs before commit.
Lock critical files during pipeline generation.
requires-engineering: add automated merge/conflict checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can generate pipeline artifacts and metadata, and Copilot can turn repo context into edits. If Copilot treats Dagster-produced files as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or configuration. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary, but human review in Workspace reduces blast radius, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace consumes Dagster-generated artifacts as source of truth, THEN downstream edits may replicate upstream mistakes.
IF a human approves Copilot-applied edits without checking Dagster outputs, THEN errors can propagate into committed code.
mitigations: Require independent verification of Dagster outputs.
Compare generated artifacts against source data.
Keep Copilot in suggestion-only mode for critical files.
Add tests that fail on malformed pipeline metadata.
requires-engineering: add schema validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and appears local-only, while Copilot is closed-source and sends editor context to GitHub/Microsoft services. If regulated or EU data is present in Dagster-managed files, Copilot creates a residency and retention mismatch. The other agent is not cited for residency because Dagster has no stated external processing path.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is present in repo context opened by Copilot, THEN it may leave the local environment.
IF the organization lacks a DPA or approved transfer mechanism for GitHub Copilot, THEN compliance exposure exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot-visible files.
Use a separate compliant environment for sensitive repos.
Review vendor transfer terms before enabling Copilot.
Limit Copilot to non-regulated projects.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware workspace routing.
